activity.notes: Representative late-fourth-century intellectual point, not an exact dated event. Oxford places Asaṅga in the fourth century; a recent specialist review of the traditional biographical sources notes Xuanzang's account of Asaṅga's activity at Ayodhya. ATLAS joins that reviewed Ayodhya activity context to the Gupta-period political frame and records active_in, not political office or court service. The c.390 point is deliberately approximate.

sources.title: Oxford Bibliographies in Buddhism — Asaṅga
sources.citation_text: Oxford describes Asaṅga as probably born in Puruṣapura in the fourth century CE and as a central systematizer of Yogācāra.

sources.title: Asaṅga: Great Systematizer of Yogācāra Thought
sources.citation_text: The specialist review summarizes Xuanzang's account that Asaṅga was active at Ayodhya and taught there.

sources.title: The Gupta Empire (AD 400–500) — The Cambridge History of Strategy
sources.citation_text: Cambridge characterizes the imperial Guptas as the dominant power in India during the fourth and fifth centuries, providing the political frame used for the reviewed Ayodhya attribution.

review_context.polity_inference: Spatiotemporal attribution: reviewed traditional source places intellectual activity at Ayodhya in the fourth-century career; Gupta political control is used at dynasty/state level. No political service is asserted.
